question: In the markdown, do the heading levels form a clean outline with no skipped level and no heading that repeats the page title or sits over nothing, and does each heading name in a few words the topic its section covers?

In the markdown and the PNG, is each inline span marked for its role: code for identifiers, paths, commands and literal values and nothing else, bold only for a lead term or key phrase and never a whole sentence, and link text that names its target?

In the markdown and the PNG, does each list use numbered items only for a sequence, task items only for work someone ticks off and nesting only for a true parent-child relation, with sibling items parallel in grammar and level of detail? Score 10 when the page has no list.

In the markdown and the PNG, does each callout's tone and printed label match the force of its message, does any title add what the label and body do not, and does the body state that one message in one or two sentences that need no surrounding prose? Score 10 when the page has no callout.

In the PNG only, can a scanning reader tell each list item's nesting depth, its siblings, whether it is bulleted, numbered or a task, and whether a task is done, from marker shape, counter, indent and hanging alignment alone? Score 10 when the page has no list.

In the PNG only, does each callout stand apart from body prose, show its tone by icon and printed label as well as by color, and keep its head line from reading as a section heading? Score 10 when the page has no callout.
